## Why this name

- Computes (b & 0xF) << 12 and merges it into a->unk14 under the mask 0xFFF, i.e. writes bits 12-15 and preserves the low 12
- Bits 12-15 of a GBA 16-bit screen entry are the palette bank, and unk14 is exactly such an entry (low 12 bits = tile index plus H/V flip)
- Sibling TextSetPaletteBank writes the same (a & 15) << 12 into the engine's global bank at gUnk_03000798->unk96; this one applies it to a single entry
- Callers pass real palette banks: sub_08037318 uses 0x0E (14), sub_0802D6D4 applies bank 2 across a run of entries
